title: Thread pool deadlock: parent join()s child in same pool, pool segregation fix, virtual threads
keyPoints: Thread pool deadlock occurs when parent tasks submit child tasks to the same pool and then call child.get(), blocking all workers and preventing children from executing.
With a pool of N workers and N parent tasks each waiting on a child, all workers are blocked and children are queued forever: permanent deadlock.
Fix 1: pool segregation (bulkhead) with separate pools for parent and child tasks so parents cannot exhaust child workers.
Fix 2: non-blocking pipelines using CompletableFuture.thenCompose() instead of submit() plus get() so no thread blocks.
Fix 3: virtual threads (Java 21) where blocking unmounts the virtual thread from its carrier, freeing the carrier for child tasks.
This is a resource exhaustion deadlock: bounded threads are the resource held by parents while waiting for children that need those same threads.
The general rule is: never submit and join in the same bounded pool.

s1_definition.oneliner: Thread pool deadlock happens when parent tasks submit children to the same bounded pool and block on child.get(), exhausting all workers so children can never execute.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Pool deadlock** – all workers in a bounded pool are occupied by parent tasks waiting on `child.get()`. Child tasks are queued in the pool's work queue but no worker is available to execute them. This is permanent deadlock with zero progress.
- **Resource exhaustion** – worker threads are finite resources. Parents hold workers while waiting for children that need those same workers. Classic resource-exhaustion deadlock pattern.
- **Pool segregation** – parents on pool-A, children on pool-B. Parents cannot exhaust child workers because they are in separate pools.
- **Non-blocking** – replace `submit() + get()` with `CompletableFuture.thenCompose()`. No thread blocks; the pipeline is driven by callbacks.
- **Virtual threads** – Java 21 virtual threads unmount from their carrier when blocked, freeing the carrier for other tasks. Blocking is effectively free, so pool exhaustion cannot occur.
s1_definition.analogy: Ten tellers at National Bank of India (pool of 10). Each teller takes a customer form (parent task) and sends a sub-form to the back office (child task) in the SAME pool. Each teller then WAITS for the back office reply. But the back office uses the SAME 10 tellers. All 10 are waiting, nobody is available for back office work: deadlock. Fix: separate front office (10 tellers) and back office (5 clerks).

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Thread Pool Deadlock
  ════════════════════

  Pool (4 workers):
  ┌────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┐
  │Parent-1│Parent-2│Parent-3│Parent-4│  ← all workers occupied
  │get()   │get()   │get()   │get()   │  ← all WAITING on children
  └────────┴────────┴────────┴────────┘

  Queue: [Child-1][Child-2][Child-3][Child-4]  ← no worker available!
  → PERMANENT DEADLOCK

  Fix: Pool Segregation
  ParentPool: [P1 get()][P2 get()][P3 get()][P4 get()]
  ChildPool:  [C1 runs][C2 runs][C3 runs][C4 runs]  ← separate workers!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Thread pool deadlock occurs when parent tasks submit children to the same bounded pool and block on child.get(). All workers become parents waiting for children that need those same workers: permanent deadlock with zero progress. This is a resource exhaustion deadlock where threads are the finite resource.

Three fixes exist. Pool segregation puts parents and children in separate pools so parents cannot exhaust child workers. Non-blocking pipelines using CompletableFuture.thenCompose() avoid blocking entirely. Virtual threads (Java 21) make blocking cheap by unmounting from the carrier, freeing it for other tasks.

At National Bank of India, a loan approval system with a 10-thread pool deadlocked because each parent submitted 3 children (credit check, property valuation, income verification) to the same pool and called get(). After introducing separate parent and child pools, the deadlock was eliminated.

Remember one sentence: never submit and join in the same bounded pool because all workers can become parents waiting for children that can never execute.
